name: Drag and drop
description: Standard drag and drop for reordering items and moving them between areas: a floating preview follows the pointer, drop targets show hover states (ready, over, reject), and a primary line indicates the exact drop position. Fully accessible with arrow keys.

classes.ayy-draggable: An item that can be picked up: grab cursor, dims to 0.4 opacity while dragging ([data-dragging]).
classes.ayy-drag-handle: The six-dot grip button: control-sized square, touch-action: none, grab cursor, takes arrow keys.
classes.ayy-sortable: Flex column container for sortable items with standard gap.
classes.ayy-sortable--horizontal: Horizontal flex layout for sortable strips, toolbars or tabs.
classes.ayy-sortable__item: Row in a sortable list: surface background, line border, dashed when dragged.
classes.ayy-drop-target: An area items can be dropped into: reacts with [data-drop="ready|over|reject"].
classes.ayy-drag-preview: Floating clone or element following the pointer in the top layer.
classes.ayy-drag-preview--chip: Compact pill-shaped preview showing the dragged item's name.

default.looks: Hidden preview; items and drop targets sit at rest.

hover.looks: Grip handle takes wash-hover and text colour.

pressed.looks: Grip handle switches to cursor: grabbing.

focus.looks: 2px ring outline on the handle; takes arrow keys.

error.looks: Rejected target gets dashed destructive border and not-allowed cursor; preview gets dashed destructive outline.

dragging.looks: Item is held: dims to 0.4 opacity with dashed line border.

ready.looks: Target accepts the item: dashed text-soft border and wash fill.

over.looks: Pointer is over target: solid primary border, 8% primary tint and 3px glow ring.

edge.looks: A 2px primary insertion line on the target edge (block-start/end, inline-start/end) showing where the item lands.

sizes.density: DragHandle sizes follow control size tokens (--ayy-size-control-sm); list items follow text and padding tokens.
sizes.width: Fills its container. Horizontally oriented lists flow inline.

js: connectDragDrop(root, options) wires pointer and keyboard dragging; setDropState(target, state) sets data-drop; setDropEdge(item, edge) sets data-drop-edge; dragPreviewChip(label) creates a chip preview; dragHandleIcon (Hugeicons DragDropVertical SVG markup).

attributes.areas: CSS selector for drop areas, e.g. .ayy-drop-target

events.ayy-move: Fired on drop or arrow key move ({ item, from, to, fromIndex, toIndex, itemId, fromId, toId })

react.import: import { Sortable, SortableItem, DragHandle, DragDropArea, DropTarget } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

a11y: Keyboard support: focused .ayy-drag-handle takes arrow keys (along the list to reorder, across to hop between areas); plain items take Alt + arrows.
Screen readers: announce polite status updates on each move ("Item moved to position 2 of 4").
DragHandle button requires an aria-label naming the specific item ('Move Revenue', 'Move Priority'); its tooltip remains general ('Drag to reorder').
do: Use drag and drop for user-driven reordering of lists, board columns, or table columns.
Always provide a DragHandle or keyboard alternative with visible focus ring.
Show clear drop indicators (ready, over, reject, and drop-edge line) so the user always knows what will happen on release.
Keep DragHandle tooltips general ('Drag to reorder'), naming the item in aria-label.
dont: Don't rely on mouse drag as the only way to reorder — always support keyboard navigation or move actions.
Don't hide the original item completely while dragging — keep it dimmed at 0.4 opacity to maintain spatial context.
Don't make drop targets ambiguous: use data-drop='reject' when an area refuses an item.
